discovery: Femtosecond optical control of magnetism: ultrafast demagnetization and all-optical magnetic switching

nominees.name: Eric Beaurepaire
nominees.affiliation: IPCMS, CNRS and University of Strasbourg, France

motivation: In 1996 Beaurepaire and co-workers showed that a femtosecond laser pulse quenches the magnetization of nickel within a picosecond, orders of magnitude faster than spin-lattice relaxation had been thought to allow. This overturned the accepted timescales of magnetism and created the field of ultrafast spin dynamics. Kimel and Rasing then showed that light can control magnetic order, not only destroy it. They excited coherent magnons non-thermally through the inverse Faraday effect, and they demonstrated all-optical helicity-dependent and thermal single-pulse magnetization switching in ferrimagnets, without any applied magnetic field. These experiments established light as a deterministic tool for writing magnetic states. They opened a new spectroscopic window on how spin, electron and lattice degrees of freedom exchange angular momentum, and they underpin today's terahertz and optical control of antiferromagnets, 2D magnets and multiferroics. The results have been reproduced widely and point toward energy-efficient, ultrafast data storage.
